ideas.title: Calibrated selection head trained on the library's blinded benchmark verdicts
ideas.sketch: Extend the idea library so each past finalist (not only the top 3) stores a fixed feature vector x: per-criterion critic scores, internal Bradley-Terry strength from the pairwise finals, development-stage score change, generator/role id, embedding distance to the nearest library idea, and nuisance covariates (card word count, number of hedges/citations, judge-model-family match). For each benchmarked brief, label finalists with the blinded external outcome: win/loss against the baseline agent's self-selected top-3 cards (humans or measured outcomes weighted 3x over the LLM panel). To get about 10 labels per brief rather than 3, run the counterbalanced panel on all finalists once. Fit an L2-regularised logistic model P(beats baseline | x) = sigmoid(w.x) with leave-one-brief-out cross-validation, and replace the final top-3 cut with ranking by predicted external win probability. Because length and polish enter as explicit covariates, the model can learn to discount judge-pleasing features instead of rewarding them. The ablation is a switch, select_by = internal_BT | calibrated. It is measured by held-out log-loss/AUC of each selector against external verdicts and by the benchmark top-3 win rate on unseen briefs. A lone agent cannot do this: it never learns how its own picks fared, so it has no labelled record of its selection error to correct.

ideas.title: Judge-reliability Bradley-Terry: per-judge discrimination and position bias learned from held-out external outcomes
ideas.sketch: In the scoring module, replace the uniform pairwise-finals Bradley-Terry with a judge-aware model, P(i beats k | judge j, i shown first) = sigmoid(a_j(theta_i - theta_k) + b_j), where j indexes judge model x prompt variant, a_j is that judge's discrimination and b_j its position bias. Estimate a_j and b_j on past library runs, anchoring theta to the external blinded verdicts, i.e. the rater/outcome rankings of the same ideas, by maximum likelihood with an N(1, 0.5) prior on a_j and N(0, 0.5) on b_j. Freeze them for new runs. Judges with a_j near zero or negative (those tracking style or their own model family rather than what raters prefer) are down-weighted automatically. The state machine then allocates the fixed finals comparison budget in proportion to a_j^2 (Fisher information per vote), and among pairs picks those whose theta difference is small near the top-3 boundary. The ablation is a switch between the uniform-weight judge panel and learned weights, at equal comparison count. It is measured by held-out pairwise agreement with external raters, the rank correlation of theta with outcome, and the benchmark top-3 win rate. The gain targets selection: a single agent is effectively one judge of unknown reliability picking its own top 3, whereas this system learns empirically which of its judges predict independent preference.
